chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-Abbas, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi Khalid, said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed that Hajj be performed on his behalf in a general manner, so he said: 'Hajj is performed on his behalf with whatever remains of his third.'

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.مُبْهَمًا: In a general or unspecified manner

ai.seo_question: How is the cost of Hajj deducted from the estate if the deceased made a general bequest for it?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifying the execution of a general Hajj bequest, ruling that it is fulfilled from the one-third share of the estate after settling debts and other bequests. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that specific religious obligations like Hajj take precedence in the distribution of the deceased's remaining assets, ensuring the spiritual debt is discharged before general inheritance distribution.
